DesktopSpotlight/Resources/DefaultCreati: In the archipelago-studded waters of the Java Sea north of Australia are the Lesser Sunda Islands. Though this chain is indeed smaller than the Greater Sunda Islands, which include such big names as Java, Sumatra, and Borneo, the Lesser Sundas do include a number of well-known places. Bali is among them, as are Lombok and Timor. One of the archipelago's smaller islands, Komodo, may also ring a bell because of the supersized lizards who roam the place.
Nusa Penida Island, Indonesia\r\n© miniloc / iStock / Getty Images Plus\r\nRight-click to learn more

Ancient civilizations used this mountain perch in the south of the Iberian Peninsula as a strategic location for fortified settlements, with Romans, Moors, and Visigoths each contributing to the modern-day Spanish city we now call Ronda.
Ronda, Spain\r\n© Marcp_dmoz on Flickr / Getty Images\r\nRight-click to learn more

Corinthia is a regional unit of Greece, located in the Peloponnese region. Those are the dry geographical facts, but the region's historical legacy is an altogether more interesting story. World powers began battling for control over this area thousands of years ago. Most were eyeing the strategic Corinth Isthmus connecting the Peloponnese peninsula to mainland Greece. The Ancient Greeks attempted to carve a passage through the land bridge (where's Zeus when you need him?) for an easier transit of the 8,320-square-mile peninsula. It wasn’t until 1893 that technology caught up with ambition and a canal was dug for maritime passage. The ensuing development in the region has led parts of Corinthia to become essentially suburbs of Athens.
A pier in Corinthia, Greece\r\nilias beros/ 500px Prime / Getty Images\r\nRight-click to learn more

Although visitors to this place may feel like they're a world away, they're actually only a stone's throw from urban hustle and bustle. Just beyond the western edge of Kyoto, Japan, lies the district of Arashiyama. The area is well known for beautiful natural scenery and attractions, including the Sagano Bamboo Forest. A walk along the paths of the forest is not just a visual treat, with daylight filtering through the thousands of green bamboo trunks, but a delight for the ears as well. As the wind blows through the forest, it creates a distinctive sound that is often cited as one of the most memorable aspects of the forest.
Sagano Bamboo Forest, Kyoto, Japan\r\n© Piriya Photography / Moment / Getty Images\r\nRight-click to learn more
DesktopSpotlight/Resources/DefaultVideoC: Arches National Park has not only thousands of arches, but also gigantic sandstone fins, massive balanced rocks, soaring pinnacles, and surreal spires. Seen here as gathering storm clouds roll past a Utah sunset, Delicate Arch rises 52 feet high, and its shape has inspired whimsical nicknames: 'The Chaps' and 'Mary's Bloomers' are just two descriptive ones bestowed by cowboys long ago. Rock climbers were once allowed to scale Delicate Arch, but that's no longer permitted for any named arch in the park. It does host temporary residents, though: white-throated swifts make their nests up top every summer.
Arches National Park, Utah, US\r\n© Thomas Brand/Creatas Video+/Getty Images Plus\r\nRight-click to learn more

Consisting of hundreds of lagoon islands connected by some 400 or so bridges, Venice remains a unique treasure beloved by residents—and beset by hordes of tourists during the high season. Quiet evening scenes such as this can still be had, though, if you wander through the backstreets and over the bridges after the tour groups and cruise ships have departed. And if you'd rather go waterborne than walk, public waterbuses called vaporetti offer rides throughout the city's historic canals.
Venice canals, Venice\r\n© BlackBoxGuild/Creatas Video+/Getty Images Plus\r\nRight-click to learn more

Ancient civilizations used this mountain perch in the south of the Iberian Peninsula as a strategic location for fortified settlements, with Romans, Moors, and Visigoths each contributing to the modern-day Spanish city we now call Ronda. Puente Nuevo is the bridge we see in the center of this video. It's one of three bridges that straddle El Tajo canyon, the gap that separates Ronda's two halves. Spilling over a steep fall beneath Puente Nuevo, the Guadalevín River supplies Ronda with water and, these days, another breathtaking scene to delight visitors.
Ronda, Spain\r\n© Marcp_dmoz on Flickr / Getty Images\r\nRight-click to learn more

Although visitors to this place may feel like they're a world away, they're actually only a stone's throw from urban hustle and bustle. At the western edge of Kyoto, Japan, lies Arashiyama, an area well known for beautiful natural scenery and attractions, including the Sagano Bamboo Forest. A walk along the paths of the forest is not just a visual treat—with daylight filtering through the thousands of green mōsōbamboo trunks—but a delight for the ears as well. As the wind blows through the bamboo, it creates a distinctive sound that is often cited as one of the most memorable aspects of the forest.
Sagano Bamboo Forest, Kyoto, Japan\r\n© Piriya Photography / Moment / Getty Images\r\nRight-click to learn more

We're soaring above the shore of Nusa Penida Island, a small member of the Lesser Sunda Islands. Though this archipelago is indeed smaller than the Greater Sunda Islands—which include such big names as Java, Sumatra, and Borneo—the Lesser Sundas do include a number of well-known places like Bali, Lombok, and Timor. One of the archipelago's smaller islands, Komodo, may also ring a bell because of the supersized lizards that roam the place. As for Nusa Penida, it may be relatively tiny, but it attracts outsized attention for its growing ecotourism and scuba opportunities.
© Thomas Brand / Creatas Video+ / Getty Images Plus

Known for its dramatic cliffs, dense rainforests, and cascading waterfalls, this UNESCO World Heritage Site is a treasure trove of natural beauty and biodiversity. Among the most iconic features of Blue Mountains National Park are its towering eucalyptus forests. The nature reserve is home to roughly 90 species of eucalyptus and offers visitors a chance to marvel at these resilient trees, which are essential to the survival of Australian wildlife. Their aromatic leaves provide food for koalas, while their bark and canopy create habitats for countless birds and insects.
Blue Mountains National Park, Australia\r\n© Thomas Brand / Creatas Video+ / Getty Images Plus\r\nRight-click to learn more
© Carl Finkbeiner / Moment Video RF / Getty Images

When the Stuart family built their Georgian estate here in the 1770s, they envisioned a long row of imposing beech trees lining the drive to their home's entrance. After two centuries, roughly 90 of the original 150 trees remain standing in a dark tangle of huge, intertwining branches that loom above a narrow road in County Antrim. The moody atmosphere has inspired more than one ghost story. And it's lured more than one film crew—most notably for an episode of 'Game of Thrones.' The tourist throngs followed, and conservation efforts (including the closing of the road to car traffic) were needed to preserve the shadowy beauty of the Dark Hedges.
County Antrim, Northern Ireland\r\n© Carl Finkbeiner / Moment Video RF / Getty Images\r\nRight-click to learn more
© ablokhin / Creatas Video+ / Getty Images Plus

Within Holland Park's 54 acres you can find myriad flower plantings, open lawns, and swathes of woodlands thick with mature trees. Keep exploring and you'll discover the small but exquisite Kyoto Garden, a gift given to London in 1991 from the city of Kyoto in Japan. A waterfall, koi pond, maple trees, and stone lanterns create a space of meditative harmony within the broader parklands. Peacocks often wander the grounds, adding to the garden's tranquil atmosphere, while carefully arranged rocks and thoughtfully placed plantings reflect traditional Japanese landscape design. Despite sitting in the heart of a bustling city, the garden feels remarkably secluded and serene.
Kyoto Japanese Garden, London\r\n© ablokhin / Creatas Video+ / Getty Images Plus\r\nRight-click to learn more

FeatureDiscoverability/Resources/Magnifi:
Press Ctrl+Alt+Minus (-) to zoom out to 1x. Press again to return to your previous zoom level- helping you save time when doing detailed work.

The shortcut works in full-screen, lens and docked modes. You can also use the “reset” button next to the “zoom in” button in the Magnifier UI to instantly switch zoom levels.
Quickly toggle between current zoom and 1x zoom

Turn on a contrast theme to reduce glare and light sensitivity, with the default set to the Aquatic dark theme. Unlike inverting colors, your images and media stay unaffected, and you can use it together with or independently of invert colors for a more comfortable view. Enable it directly from the Magnifier toolbar: open Magnifier settings and flip the contrast theme toggle. To pick which contrast theme is used by default, go to Accessibility > Magnifier > Appearance.
Use contrast themes in magnifier for a more comfortable display
We've refreshed the Magnifier toolbar with a more modern, cleaner design with updated icons, spacing, and padding for a clearer, more comfortable interface.

Locking freezes cursor tracking and the magnified viewport stops panning while locked so you can stay focused on the magnified content that matters while working on another screen in multi monitor setups. Press Ctrl + Win + K to lock or unlock a display or alternatively use Win + Esc to unlock all displays. You can choose an alternate keyboard shortcut under Accessibility > Magnifier > Multiple display controls.
Lock the content that matters to you in multi display setups

Magnifier now offers natural voices, including new high-definition options for even clearer, lifelike speech-helping you enjoy a smoother reading experience. To get started, download your preferred voice from <link Id="MagnifierSettings" InboxUri="true">Settings -> Accessibility -> Magnifier.</link>

Natural voices are available in multiple languages and HD voices are currently available in English (United states). You can change voices or adjust speed anytime in Magnifier settings.
Hear text clearly with natural voices

Magnifier now lets you customize the zoom level to the exact value of choice for a more precise and natural zoom experience. You can now click and type in the zoom level of your choice on the magnifier bar.  

You can now also modify zoom increments directly from the magnifier bar instead of navigating to Windows Settings each time. Simply press the gear icon on the magnifier bar, navigate to the 'zoom increment option' to change by what increments you'd prefer magnifier to zoom in and out by.
Fine tune your desired zoom level

Magnifier now lets you set a different zoom level for each display, helping you move between screens without readjusting magnification. You can turn this feature on or off under Accessibility > Magnifier > Multiple display controls.
Use a different zoom level on each display

Touch bars for panning are now off by default. If you use a touch screen device and prefer on-screen bars for navigating your magnified view, you can turn them on anytime in <link Id="MagnifierSettings" InboxUri="true">Settings > Accessibility > Magnifier.</link>
Touch bars are now off by default

FeatureDiscoverability/Resources/Narrato: Narrator now offers a new AI-powered feature that enhances accessibility by providing detailed image descriptions across Windows. Simply press Narrator key+Ctrl+D and Narrator will provide contextual details, describing people, objects, colors, and even settings within the image. This feature is only available on Copilot+ PCs.

We have addressed issues with the Narrator's performance after extended use. This improvement would allow you to continuously use Narrator without it slowing down over time.

Click to <link Id="LearnMore">learn more</link>

Narrator now includes high-definition voices for more natural, lifelike speech- making it easier to follow text comfortably. To get started, download your preferred voice from <link Id="NarratorSettings" InboxUri="true">Narrator settings.</link>

These HD voices are currently available in English (United States) with one male and one female option. You can switch voices or adjust speed anytime in Narrator settings.

Narrator now supports HID-based braille displays making it easier to get started with plug-and-play connectivity. Simply connect your compatible braille display using USB or Bluetooth and Narrator will recognize it automatically. No additional drivers are required. Once connected, text appears on your refreshable braille display and updates automatically as you move and use Windows. For Bluetooth, pair your braille display just like a keyboard or headphones in Bluetooth and devices settings. Once connected, Narrator will begin using your display. If your display is not detected, check your connection or try reconnecting your device. You can also customize braille input and output anytime in Configure Braille Displays settings. To learn more about using braille with Narrator, refer our Narrator guide.

When you are focused on any control, like a button, checkbox, or list item, you can adjust which details Narrator announces for that control type, such as its name, position info, state, value etc. Press Narrator key+Alt+P to open personalization for the control you are currently on. You can choose which properties Narrator should announce, reorder them, and use Preview to hear the updated announcement before applying your changes. Select Reset to default anytime to restore the original order. Your changes apply to this control type throughout the app.

When you are focused on any control, like a button, checkbox, or list item, you can adjust which details Narrator announces for that control type, such as its name, position info, state, value etc. Press Narrator key+Alt+P to open personalization for the control you are currently on. You can choose which properties to announce, reorder them, or type a natural instruction like "Don't announce the selection info or position info." Use Preview to hear the updated announcement before applying your changes, and select Reset to default the original order. Your changes apply to this control type throughout the app.

Narrator now works with Copilot to describe images and visual elements on your screen using AI. Press Narrator key+Ctrl+D to describe the focused image, or Narrator key+Ctrl+W to describe the full screen. Copilot opens with the image ready—just enter your prompt to generate a description. You stay in control: the image is only shared after you choose to describe it.

On Copilot+ PCs, Narrator uses AI to describe images locally—highlighting people, objects, colors, and settings. Press Narrator key+Ctrl+D to hear the description instantly. For more details or follow-up questions, press the Ask Copilot button. The image is only shared after you choose to describe it using your own prompt.

Narrator can now read math equations in supported apps, including Word and PowerPoint. Instead of reading every symbol individually, Narrator describes equations in a natural way that makes them easier to understand. For example, when you reach a fraction, Narrator reads the numerator and denominator so you can understand the relationship between them. To explore an equation in more detail, press Narrator key+Alt+N to turn on math navigation. Use the arrow keys to move through different parts of the equation, such as fractions, exponents, and roots. This lets you explore the equation one part at a time. Press Escape to exit math navigation. You can select your preferred language for math reading in Math reading settings. To learn more about using Narrator to read and explore math equations, refer the Narrator guide.

Narrator now gives you faster access to essential email and meeting details in Outlook, so you can hear the information you need on demand without needing to navigate through every field in the UI. In an email: With Narrator on, open a message and press a number shortcut to hear a specific detail. Press Alt+1 for the sender, Alt+2 for the date, Alt+3 for recipients, Alt+4 for Cc, Alt+5 for the subject, Alt+6 for Bcc, and Alt+7 for attachments. In a meeting: With Narrator on, open a meeting from your calendar and press a number shortcut to hear a specific detail. Press Alt+1 for the organizer, Alt+2 for the date, Alt+3 for required attendees, Alt+4 for optional attendees, Alt+5 for the subject, Alt+7 for attachments, Alt+8 for the meeting time, and Alt+9 for the meeting location. These experiences work through Narrator extensions, which are turned on by default. If they do not work for you, make sure Enable Narrator extensions is turned on in Narrator settings.

You can now turn off Narrator speech whenever you need silence, without stopping Narrator. Press Narrator key+Shift+S to toggle speech off. Press the same shortcut again to turn speech back on. This is useful in situations where Narrator's speech might overlap with what you're hearing, such as during meetings, while listening to audio or video, or when using self-voicing apps. If you prefer reading with Braille alone, you can turn off speech and rely entirely on your display. Braille output continues to work normally while speech is off, so you won't miss any information. Narrator stays fully active, only the spoken output is paused. Speech returns to its normal state the next time you start Narrator. Your verbosity and voice settings are not affected.

Narrator now helps you review and edit documents in Microsoft Word more efficiently, so you can check your writing and work through comments with fewer keystrokes. Check spelling and grammar: With Narrator on, press F7 to start spellcheck. Narrator announces the type of issue, the word in error, the surrounding context, and each available suggestion, and it slows down briefly when spelling out the misspelled word so it is easier to follow. To fix an issue, press 1 to apply the first suggestion, 2 to apply the second, and so on. Press i to ignore once, g to ignore all, or a to add the word to your dictionary. Read and work through comments: When your cursor is on text that contains a comment, press Alt+Shift+' to hear the full context of the comment, including the author's name, any assigned task, and the number of replies, without leaving your place in the document. To work with the comment, press Alt+F12 to move into the comment card, then press Alt+Shift+' again to hear the commented text, so you always know which part of the document the comment refers to. If there is no comment on the selected text, Narrator tells you clearly. These experiences work through Narrator extensions, which are turned on by default. If they do not work for you, make sure Enable Narrator extensions is turned on in Narrator settings.

FeatureDiscoverability/Resources/PageCon:
We have some new updates to voice access, including enhanced speech recognition and extended language support.

Click Next to learn about other new updates to voice access.

Voice shortcuts are now part of your command library and you can create them for actions like pasting predefined text and media, or even performing a sequence of actions. Simply say "Create shortcut" to get started.

Spell mode performance has been improved, along with enabling dictation commands like "Delete line".

Simply say "spell that" to start spelling a new word or say "correct that" to get the improved suggestions based on your active word selection.

Say the command "Add to vocabulary" to add the words you find challenging to dictate. Using the command immediately after correcting, or spelling a word would add it instantly to your vocabulary. 
You can alternatively add words from voice access settings menu as well.

We are leveraging AI processing on your PC to make intent recognition better and offer real-time command suggestions.

Interacting with voice access is much more intuitive than before.

Voice access automatically corrects punctuation, capitalization, grammar, and common spelling mistakes. You can control it by saying “Turn on/Turn off fluid dictation”. To undo the latest correction, say “Revert." Please make sure to always review the text, as AI-generated corrections can sometimes be inaccurate. This feature is now available only for English.

Improve word recognition by adding difficult words to your vocabulary anywhere with the command "Add to vocabulary". Use the command immediately after correcting or spelling a word to instantly add the word.  

You can also access the vocabulary builder from voice access settings menu.
To control when speech processing begins, select Wait time before acting in voice access settings, then choose a time that fits your communication style.
Voice isolation helps recognize your voice even in noisy or shared spaces. Go to Improve speech recognition and set up Voice isolation to help voice access understand you better.
